title: Can, must, want
title_target: Je peux, je dois, je veux
goal: Ask for permission, say what you must and want to do, and make plans with aller + infinitive.
bekal: talking about the future with *je vais* + infinitive
wave: Review **Unit 14** first: pick five pieces of clothing in your closet, say their colors in the right form, then point to each one with *ce*, *cet*, *cette*, or *ces*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Les papiers de l'étranger
dialogs.intro: Budi is sorting out his residence permit. Camille goes with him to the prefecture.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Je dois renouveler mon titre de séjour ce mois-ci.
lines.id: I have to renew my residence permit this month.
lines.literal: I must renew my permit of stay this month-here.

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Tu peux prendre rendez-vous en ligne, c'est plus simple.
lines.id: You can make an appointment online, it's easier.
lines.literal: you can take appointment in line, it-is more simple.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: J'ai essayé, mais il n'y a pas de place avant mai.
lines.id: I tried, but there are no slots before May.
lines.literal: I have tried, but there not-is not of place before May.

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Alors il faut y aller très tôt le matin.
lines.id: Then you have to go very early in the morning.
lines.literal: then it is-needed there go very early the morning.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: À quelle heure ? Je ne veux pas rater le cours.
lines.id: What time? I don't want to miss class.
lines.literal: at what hour? I not want not miss the course.

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Vers sept heures. Tu dois apporter tous tes papiers.
lines.id: Around seven. You have to bring all your papers.
lines.literal: toward seven hours. you must bring all your papers.

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Ton passeport, ton attestation, et une photo récente.
lines.id: Your passport, your certificate, and a recent photo.
lines.literal: your passport, your certificate, and a photo recent.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Je peux faire une photo à la gare, je crois.
lines.id: I can get a photo taken at the station, I think.
lines.literal: I can make a photo at-the station, I believe.

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Oui. Et n'oublie pas : il ne faut pas arriver en retard.
lines.id: Yes. And remember: you mustn't be late.
lines.literal: yes. and forget not: it not is-needed not arrive in lateness.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Je vais mettre trois réveils. Promis.
lines.id: I'm going to set three alarms. Promise.
lines.literal: I go set three alarms. promised.

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Je vais venir avec toi. On va y arriver.

notes: **These three verbs are always followed by an infinitive.** *Je peux **partir***, *je dois **travailler***, *je veux **manger***. The infinitive never changes, whoever the subject is — far simpler than beginners fear, and just like "I can leave", "I must work".

**Il faut = you have to, but with no subject.** Literally "it is needed". Used for general obligations that apply to anyone: *il faut arriver tôt* (you have to arrive early — anyone does). Compare *tu dois arriver tôt* (you in particular must).

**⚠️ Il ne faut pas means "you mustn't", not "you don't have to".** This is a big trap. *Il ne faut pas fumer* = no smoking. To say "you don't need to", use *ce n'est pas nécessaire* or *tu n'as pas besoin de*.
**Je ne dois pas also means "I mustn't"** in many contexts, just like English *must not*. If you mean "I don't have to", say *je ne suis pas obligé de*.

**Je vais + infinitive** is the most common way to talk about the future in everyday French, just like "I'm going to…". The real future tense (*futur simple*) comes at A2, and the French themselves use *aller* more in conversation.
**En ligne** = online. A modern phrase that's now in the official dictionary. Its cousins: *sur Internet*, *sur le site*.
**On va y arriver** = "we'll make it". A very common phrase of encouragement, literally "one is going to arrive there".

grammars.title: Pouvoir, devoir, vouloir
body: Three verbs that look alike — and all three change their stem in the *nous* and *vous* forms.
after: Notice the pattern: the three singular forms sound the same (*peux, peux, peut* = PUH), then the stem changes for *nous* and *vous*, then changes again for *ils*. Exactly the same pattern for all three.
The negative wraps around **the first verb** only: *je ne peux pas venir*, not *je ne peux venir pas*.
Polite forms you must master: *je voudrais* (I would like), *pourriez-vous…?* (could you…?), *est-ce que je pourrais…?* (could I…?).

grammars.title: Four ways to express obligation
body: All of them come out as "must" or "have to" in English, but the tone differs.
after: The third row uses the *subjonctif*, which isn't taught at A1. Just recognize it as a phrase; don't build it yourself.
*Avoir besoin de* takes *de*, and that *de* merges as usual: *j'ai besoin **du** livre*, *j'ai besoin **des** clés*.

grammars.title: Talking about the future
body: One pattern covers everything you need at A1: a form of *aller* + infinitive.
after: The negative wraps around *aller*: *je ne vais pas partir*.
Useful future time words: *demain*, *après-demain*, *la semaine prochaine*, *l'année prochaine*, *bientôt* (soon), *plus tard* (later).
For the very near future, the present tense is enough: *je pars dans cinq minutes*.

blocks.text: In French, politeness grows with the length of the sentence. The longer and more roundabout, the more polite — much like English "Could you possibly…" versus "Give me…".

blocks.title: Asking for permission
items: *Je peux entrer ?* — May I come in?
*Est-ce que je peux ouvrir la fenêtre ?* — Can I open the window?
*Ça vous dérange si je m'assois ici ?* — Do you mind if I sit here?

blocks.title: Common signs that forbid things
items: *Il est interdit de…* — It is forbidden to…
Notice that signs use the infinitive, not the imperative.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct form of the verb.
Turn into a future plan with aller.
Choose il faut or il ne faut pas.

items: I have to renew my residence permit.
You can make an appointment online.
I don't want to miss class.
I'm going to come with you.
